U0189.d: U0189 covers the third disc player or changer on the bus, module C. Systems with more than one drive are found mostly in rear-seat entertainment or luxury setups, where a front unit and separate rear players feed different screens. The head unit or another listener stores U0189 once module C's cyclic messages stop arriving; GM describes this mechanism for all U0100-U02FF codes, with voltage required to be between 9 and 16 V. No manufacturer documents U0189 publicly, and GM's published list contains no disc player codes. U0187 and U0188 name modules A and B, U0190 module D. Check whether the vehicle really has a third drive before chasing wiring. Only that source fails; no MIL, no effect on driving.

Code stored in the head unit

U0190.d: U0190 is the last code in the J2012 disc player block and names module D, a fourth networked drive or changer. When that unit goes silent, the modules expecting its periodic traffic store U0190; GM's procedure for U0100-U02FF adds that a code stored only in history after a flat battery or a module disconnected with the bus awake is not a reason to replace parts. No manufacturer documents U0190 publicly, and a fourth disc drive is very rare in practice, so the code is unusual. A changer is a mechanical unit that loads discs from a magazine, which makes power supply and mounting location the first checks. U0187 to U0189 cover modules A to C. U0215.d: U0215 means the networked door switch unit A no longer answers. In many doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are small bus nodes, usually LIN slaves under a door or body module, and the master stores this code once switch A stops replying. The manufacturer decides which door panel carries letter A. U0215 to U0221 cover switches A to G. The buttons on that panel stop working, while the other doors normally keep working.

U0219.d: U0219 means the networked door switch unit E is no longer heard. In modern doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are often small bus nodes, typically LIN slaves under a door or body module, so each panel can report its own communication loss. The master that polls switch E stores U0219 once its replies stop; GM documents this setting rule for the whole U0100-U02FF range. No manufacturer documents U0219 publicly; GM's U-code list uses its own entries (U0203/U0204) for rear door switch panel modules instead. The letter E is assigned by the maker, so the door concerned must be taken from the vehicle's documentation. U0215 to U0218 and U0220 cover the other switches. Window or lock buttons fail; no MIL.

U0304.d: U0304 is stored when a control unit, usually the transmission controller, finds that the software or calibration identity of the gear shift control module does not match what it expects. GM's generic U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) treats such codes as configuration faults: checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, no circuit test, cured by setup or programming. Allison uses U0304 for its 6th-generation controls as Gear Shift Module 1 Incompatible: a 6th-generation push-button selector does not work with a 5th-generation TCM, and the selector must match the TCM calibration; U0333 covers selector 2. U0103 means lost contact, U0404 invalid data from the same module. The driver may be unable to select a range.

U0316.d: U0316 means the vehicle dynamics control module, the electronic stability control unit, reports a software or calibration identity another module does not accept, typically after it was replaced or reflashed without setup. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) runs at 9-16 V and sets such codes when a module is not configured properly; GM itself uses U0315 for its electronic brake module. Mazda uses U0316 differently: in 2014-2015 Mazda3, Mazda6 and CX-5 bulletins U0316:09 sits in a receiving module and stands for an error signal received from the DSC unit, there caused by a failed SAS module. So on a Mazda it is a follow-up code, not a software issue. U0122 means lost contact, U0416 invalid data. Stability control may switch off; MIL normally off.
s: Stability or traction control warning light on
Code stored in several modules at once

c: Park brake module replaced or flashed without setup
Mitsubishi: CAN time-out to the EPB ECU, e.g. connector unplugged
Software level of park brake module and partner module do not match
U0317.d: U0317 tells that the park brake control module of an electric parking brake runs software or a calibration another module does not accept. Following GM's generic U03xx logic it is checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, sets when a module is not configured properly and needs no wiring test; the cure is setup or programming. No manufacturer documents this J2012 meaning publicly. Mitsubishi reassigns the number: for the 2017 Outlander (TSB-17-23-001) U0317 stands for a CAN time-out with the EPB ECU, which a wrongly programmed TCM stored as P0317 instead; a TCM reflash corrects it. On such vehicles read U0317 as a communication fault. U0128 means lost contact, U0417 invalid data. Park brake warnings or disabled auto functions are possible; no MIL.
s: Park brake warning light or message
Automatic release or hill hold not working
Code appears after park brake module work
U0317.t: Software Incompatibility With Park Brake Control Module

c: Brake system module replaced or flashed without setup
Software level does not match the ABS/ESC or engine controller
Programming aborted due to low battery voltage
U0318.d: U0318 indicates a software or calibration mismatch with the brake system control module, a unit J2012 separates from the ABS module (U0315) and the vehicle dynamics module (U0316). Which box that is depends on the maker; on brake-by-wire systems or electromechanical boosters it is often the controller that builds brake pressure. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) describes the trigger: a module not configured properly, checked at 9-16 V, no external circuit involved. No manufacturer documents U0318 publicly, so the exact owner of the code must come from the vehicle's own manual. It mostly appears after a module swap or a broken flash. U0129 means lost contact, U0418 invalid data. Brake warnings and reduced assist functions are possible; MIL usually off.
s: Brake system warning light or message
Brake assist or regenerative braking functions unavailable
Code appears after brake module service

U0401.d: The ECM/PCM is present on the data bus but the values it reports are implausible — out of range, frozen, or failing the checksum or rolling-count check. The receiving modules reject the data. Implausible engine data can force limp mode or stall the engine. Causes include a faulty sensor feeding the module, internal computation errors, a software or calibration mismatch after a repair, or bus interference corrupting the frames.

c: Corroded or loose connector, damaged bus wire to the injector module
Low supply voltage at the injector module
Software levels of injector module and ECM do not match
Injector control module internally faulty
U0406.d: U0406 means a receiving controller, normally the ECM/PCM, gets messages from the fuel injector control module that arrive but fail its checks: wrong counter, checksum, range or a signal marked invalid. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows the U04xx principle with U0401: the TCM stores it when the ECM sends invalid or faulted torque or pedal data. A separate injector module exists only on some designs; GM's 2013 bi-fuel CNG Silverado/Sierra uses an FICM that switches the injectors and passes rail pressure and temperature to the ECM over serial data. No manufacturer documents U0406 publicly. As fuel delivery affects emissions, CARB requires such inputs to be monitored and a MIL is likely. U0105 means lost contact, U0306 a software mismatch.
s: Rough running, misfire or hard start

c: LIN wire or connector between glow module and ECM corroded or loose
Glow plug control module internally faulty
Voltage dip during glow check or cranking
Glow module software does not match the ECM
U0407.d: U0407 is stored when the engine controller receives data from the glow plug control module that it rejects as implausible. Volkswagen lists the code in the 2014 Touareg diesel OBD chart as Invalid Data Received From Glow Plug Control Module 1, criterion implausible messages received. On that engine the glow unit talks to the ECM over LIN; VW uses U0106 for a missing LIN message and U0307 for a failed software check, which separates the three siblings clearly. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows the same U04xx idea for other modules: data arrive but are faulted. Because the glow module also reports plug faults, invalid data can hide real glow plug problems. Expect hard cold starts, white smoke and on a diesel usually the MIL.
s: Check engine or glow plug light on
White smoke and rough idle after cold start
U0407.t: Invalid Data Received From Glow Plug Control Module

c: Damaged bus wire or poor connector contact at the throttle module
Throttle actuator control module internally faulty
Software of throttle module and ECM do not match
Low or unstable supply voltage
U0408.d: U0408 points to messages from the throttle actuator control module that the receiver, usually the ECM/PCM, judges invalid: implausible content, a failed checksum or counter, or a value outside its range. Most vehicles integrate throttle control in the engine controller, so a separate TAC module and therefore this code are uncommon; no manufacturer documents U0408 publicly. Ford's 2012 OBD summary illustrates the U04xx logic with U0401, which the TCM stores when ECM torque or pedal data are faulted. Because the throttle meters intake air, CARB's comprehensive component rules apply, and a MIL together with reduced power or a limp mode is likely. U0107 means lost contact, U0308 a software mismatch with the same module.
s: Limp mode with reduced throttle response
U0408.t: Invalid Data Received From Throttle Actuator Control Module

c: Corroded connector or damaged wiring of the retrofit or factory gas system
Faulty gas rail pressure/temperature sensor delivering implausible values
Alternative fuel control module faulty or wrongly configured
U0409.d: U0409 is logged when the engine controller receives data from the alternative fuel control module that fail its validity checks. Such a module runs the gas side of bi-fuel CNG or LPG vehicles. In Ford's 2000 bi-fuel OBD description the AFCM passes the requested mode (ALT or GAS) and supply status between the gas metering unit and the PCM, which then switches the petrol injectors on or off; GM's 2013 CNG Silverado/Sierra sends rail pressure and temperature from its injector module to the ECM over serial data. No manufacturer documents U0409 publicly. Corrupt data can make the engine fall back to petrol or misjudge gas pressure, so CARB monitoring applies and a MIL is likely. U0108 means lost contact, U0309 a software mismatch.
s: Engine stays on or switches back to petrol
Gas gauge or fuel mode indicator incorrect

U0410.d: U0410 means the engine controller receives data from the fuel pump control module that it cannot trust, such as a bad checksum, counter or an out-of-range value. Many cars drive the in-tank pump through such a module to set the low-side pressure on demand. GM shows why the data matter for emissions: bulletin PIP5427 (2014-2016 trucks and SUVs) traces a lit service engine lamp and a fuel pressure deviation P2635 to communication faults between ECM and pump module, logged there as U0074 or GM's own U18A2. From 2014 GM renamed this unit chassis control module. No manufacturer documents U0410 publicly. Expect a MIL, hesitation or reduced power. U0109 means lost contact, U0310 a software mismatch.
s: Fuel pressure codes such as P2635 set together

c: Damaged pins or poor contact in harness connectors near the drive motor (Bentley case)
Faulty motor temperature sensor circuit making the module send invalid data
Software of motor module and hybrid controller do not match
Drive motor control module internally faulty
U0411.d: U0411 is stored when a controller, typically the engine or hybrid controller, receives messages from the drive motor control module (the inverter electronics of an electric traction motor) that it judges invalid. Volkswagen lists it in its 2014 hybrid OBD charts: for the Touareg Hybrid on implausible messages from the motor module, for the Jetta Hybrid on an incorrect CAN data length code. Bentley's Flying Spur Hybrid (2022-2023) stores U041100 in the engine control unit with a warning lamp, partly together with P0A2E for the motor temperature sensor circuit, and has the technician measure and inspect a harness connector. U0110 means lost contact, U0311 a software mismatch. Hybrid drive may be limited or switched off.
s: Engine or drive system warning light on
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs constantly

U0412.d: U0412 is stored when the hybrid or engine controller receives data from battery energy control module A, the management unit of the high-voltage battery, that it rejects as invalid. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid OBD chart sets it on implausible received data. FCA lists U0412-00 for the 2019 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid (TSB 08-114-22) among codes that light the MIL and can remain as permanent codes, so the vehicle fails a state smog check; the fix is new software for the hybrid control processors, not a battery part. CARB requires emission-related control units to be monitored, which explains the MIL. U0111 means lost contact, U0413 covers module B, U0312 a software mismatch. Charging or electric driving may be limited.
s: Check engine light on, code may become permanent

U0413.d: U0413 is the counterpart of U0412 for battery energy control module B, used where the high-voltage battery has a second management unit or a split controller. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid chart sets it on implausible data, while the 2014 Touareg Hybrid chart uses U0413 for its single battery module, which shows that the A/B assignment is maker-specific. Audi stores U041300 in the engine and electric drive controllers of the Q5 and A7 plug-in hybrids (model years 2019-2022) together with a drive system warning; the cause was software in the battery management and its junction box, cured by an update.
